extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, patent stakeholders (practitioners, industry), Congress, and policy advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Annual advisory-committee recommendations and takeaways for USPTO patent policy, operations, rulemaking, outreach, finance, patent quality, PTAB, AI, and IT management. The document gives statutory duties, performance expectations, and recommended metrics/practices for agency decision-making and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPAC statutory review duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Advisory Committee shall review the policies, goals, performance, budget, and user fees of the United States Patent and Trademark Office with respect to patents (Patent Public Advisory Committee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory duty to advise the Director on those matters; used as the baseline evaluative lens for PPAC recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report and transmission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after the end of each fiscal year: (A) prepare an annual report on the matters referred to in paragraph (1); (B) transmit the report to the Secretary of Commerce, the President, and the Committees on the Judiciary of the Senate and the House of Representatives; and (C) publish the report in the Official Gazette of the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness, transmission to specified recipients, and publication in the Official Gazette are explicit procedural and accountability requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rulemaking timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical Federal rulemaking milestones and approximate durations shown: NPRM (30 weeks) and FR (20 weeks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these timeline expectations when planning and evaluating the progress of rulemaking activities; monitor deviations and their causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track volume of Federal Register notices and public comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor the number and types of notices (Final rule, NPRM, Request for comments, Guidance) and the volume of written comments received for a fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use counts of notices and comments as a metric of rulemaking activity and public engagement (the report lists totals by type and total comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful, collaborative approach for complex rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: For especially complex rulemaking issues (e.g., PTAB Rules of Practice for Briefing Discretionary Denial Issues, Rules for 325(d) Considerations, Instituting Parallel and Serial Petitions, Termination Due to Settlement Agreement), encourage careful consideration and collaboration for a balanced solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor deliberation and stakeholder collaboration rather than rapid unilateral rule changes on complex technical/process issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase public outreach, education, and pro bono support
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue and expand public outreach, education, and pro bono support efforts to reach students, practitioners, and communities in underrepresented geographies and demographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure success by increased participation and reach; leverage NSII/OPE/COOs to build a comprehensive strategy to broaden demographic and geographic participation in the innovation ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop preliminary assessment metrics with target communities
rubrics_metrics.description: OPE should consult and collaborate with target communities and groups to develop preliminary assessment metrics to ensure the efficacy of present initiatives and inform outreach and inclusivity strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-develop metrics with stakeholders (target communities) to evaluate program outcomes and refine outreach approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate public outreach and education initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate the USPTO network of public outreach and education initiatives (through OPE and CI2) to maximize program efficiencies and outcomes and reinforce NSII objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek integration across internal and private-sector programs to avoid duplication, improve efficiency, and amplify impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set success criteria and evaluate non-examination spending
rubrics_metrics.description: Set success criteria and periodically evaluate new, non-examination spending to avoid unproductive non-examination spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require measurable success criteria for new programs and periodic reviews to ensure funds support the USPTO mission and avoid waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize spending on examination and adjudication; protect fee integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that fees collected remain in the agency and are spent predominately on the examination and adjudication of IP rights; avoid sequestration risks that divert fees to unrelated government purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for legislative and budgetary protections so patent-related fees are used for patent-related services; monitor sequestration exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renew and improve fee-setting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Support renewal of agency fee-setting authority and work to continuously improve the rationale, transparency, and objectives of future fee increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transparent rationale and clear objectives when proposing fee changes; engage PPAC and stakeholders in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure stable appropriations and access to previously collected fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Promptly enact appropriations to avoid shutdowns or continuing resolutions that force the USPTO to dip into its operating reserve; appropriate or otherwise find a way forward on approximately $950M in unavailable but previously collected patent fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative and budgetary action is needed to maintain long-term fiscal stability; monitor and advocate for solutions to inaccessible fee balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage unexamined inventory with multi-faceted approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Address unprecedented unexamined inventory through a multi-faceted approach, including massive hiring, while balancing hiring needs against the Office’s financial stability and core mission of issuing robust and reliable patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh production increases from hiring against training burdens, compensation costs, and fiscal constraints; monitor impacts on patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and prioritize examiner training during expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Care must be taken with additional hires to ensure that training (which will require additional work for current Examiners) is not curtailed, particularly given declines in patent examination satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not sacrifice training quality for throughput; track examiner satisfaction and training metrics as part of hiring plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore examiner incentive alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous incentives (gainsharing awards, 1:1) showed limited success; continue to explore additional incentive alternatives to increase production without undermining quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot and evaluate incentive programs, measure both production and quality outcomes, and publish lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study and publish PTAB invalidation data and causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent quality is undermined by the PTAB invalidation rate (over 50% for claims reviewed in Post Grant challenges); the USPTO should study this trend and publish all data and conclusions to educate stakeholders on likely causes for invalidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect, analyze, and transparently publish data on invalidation rates and causal factors to close the loop between examination and post-grant outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate causes of PTAB invalidations (search, hindsight bias, expert testimony)
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular study areas may include search capabilities, potential for hindsight bias, and the use of expert testimony during IPR proceedings consistent with statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design empirical studies focused on these mechanisms and recommend procedural or training changes if they contribute to invalidations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess impact of inequitable conduct doctrine on examination quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the doctrine of inequitable conduct, as currently applied, is encouraging behavior that decreases the quality of examination and resulting patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether current enforcement/application of inequitable conduct incentives undesirable behaviors and recommend adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider more robust use of section 325(d) to improve examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether more robust use of section 325(d), with applicable rules that would encourage patent applicants to highlight a limited number of references during examination, would improve patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess rule changes that focus applicant attention on key references to improve examination efficiency and quality; weigh against applicant burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO as a generator of robust empirical evidence (FDA study example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO should continue to generate robust, accurate, and unbiased empirical data (e.g., USPTO/FDA drug patent & exclusivity study) to inform patent policy discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain high standards of empirical research quality and objectivity; use such studies to inform regulatory and policy choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore, utilize, and advance AI in the USPTO enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC recommends the USPTO continue to explore, utilize and advance AI as it relates to being a facilitator of invention, the subject matter of invention, and a propelling tool for the USPTO enterprise effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt AI where it improves operations and services while studying implications for subject matter and examination; ensure ethical and effective deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine how AI may foster invention while preserving human-invention principle
rubrics_metrics.description: While statute, case law, and guidance provide that invention remains a human activity, PPAC encourages examination of how AI, as it evolves, may foster invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor legal boundaries and policy implications as AI capabilities change; incorporate findings into guidance and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify patent subject matter eligibility for AI and provide examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Congratulates issuance of guidance on 'Patent Subject Matter Eligibility, Including Artificial Intelligence' and encourages continuing clarification with a wider range of examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop additional illustrative examples to help examiners and applicants navigate edge cases between concrete and abstract subject matter involving AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue issuing and refining AI-related guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend the USPTO continue to issue and refine guidance documents as nuances of AI mechanisms, algorithms, and operation continue to be revealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat guidance as iterative; update as technical and legal understanding evolves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in continued training across USPTO personnel for AI and complex technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Investing in continued training of USPTO personnel—from examiner to staff to administrator—is essential to ensure issuance and stewardship of optimal, robust, quality patents in complex interdisciplinary areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate resources for ongoing technical and policy training to maintain examination quality amid technological change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen and modernize USPTO IT infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Information technology at the USPTO is a critical resource for accomplishing key goals of a robust and reliable patent system and for serving customers and users of USPTO services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue modernization projects that improve reliability, scalability, and service delivery; measure outcomes for users and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and improve cybersecurity and cloud migration strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to improve cybersecurity infrastructure, including the cloud migration strategy, to meet current cybersecurity challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize security architectures and migration plans; evaluate and report on cybersecurity posture and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage diverse users to enhance IT user experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with the diverse range of users of public IT services in order to enhance user experiences with those services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct outreach and usability research with varied user groups to inform improvements and accessibility enhancements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue IT modernization with cost containment
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO should continue its IT modernization efforts while remaining diligent about cost containment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance modernization benefits against budgetary discipline; set cost-control metrics and prioritization frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand UX testing for public IT services
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO should expand its current practices of UX testing for public IT services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase user-experience testing frequency and scope; incorporate findings into iterative design and deployment decisions.
